summary: Émilie Aussant works in indology and linguistics. She studied under Georges-Jean Pinault and held an attested post at Paris Diderot University in 2014.

Étienne Balazs was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied under Otto Franke from 1923 to 1930. He worked at the CNRS in 1949 and served as a professor at the University of Paris from circa 1950 to 1963.

Étienne Lamotte was a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology who studied at KU Leuven and in Paris and Rome. He taught at Saint-Louis University, Brussels, and held a post at KU Leuven from 1932 to 1974.

Étienne Marc Quatremère worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, he held a post at the Collège de France from 1819 to 1857.

Ñāṇavīra Thera worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, and under Pelene Siri Vajiragnana and Nyanatiloka Mahathera, after serving in the Royal Artillery and Intelligence Corps.

Ösel Tendzin was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Fordham University and under Swami Satchidananda and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as executive vice president of Vajradhatu from 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and indology who studied at the University of Tartu from 1980 to 1986. He held a post at the University of Tartu circa 1995 and has served as an editor of Numen.
Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Oberlin College and under Fuang Jotiko. He founded Metta Forest Monastery, serving as its abbot from 1993.
